title: 2025 AMC 10B Problem 9
statement:
How many ordered triples of integers \((x, y, z)\) satisfy the following system of inequalities?

\[-x - y - z \le -2\] \[-x + y + z \le 2\] \[x - y + z \le 2\] \[x + y - z \le 2\]

solutions.text: Let \(p = -x + y + z,\) \(q = x - y + z,\) \(r = x + y - z.\) The last three inequalities say \(p, q, r \le 2,\) the first says \(x + y + z \ge 2,\) and \(p + q + r = x + y + z.\) Since \(x = \tfrac{q + r}{2}\) and so on, \(p, q, r\) must all share the same parity. Now count triples with each part \(\le 2,\) equal parity, and sum in \([2, 6].\) The even ones are \((2,2,2),\) the permutations of \((2,2,0),\) of \((2,0,0),\) and of \((2,2,-2),\) giving \(10.\) The only odd one is \((1,1,1).\) That’s \(11\) in all, and each yields a unique \((x, y, z).\) Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: The last three inequalities are symmetric in \(x, y, z;\) let \(p = -x + y + z,\) \(q = x - y + z,\) \(r = x + y - z\)
Then \(p, q, r \le 2\) with equal parity and \(p + q + r = x + y + z \ge 2;\) count such triples
